answers.name: Titan
answers.fact: Bigger than Mercury, with rain and rivers made of methane.

answers.name: Enceladus
answers.fact: Sprays water from cracks at its south pole, feeding one of Saturn's rings.

answers.name: Mimas
answers.fact: Its enormous Herschel crater makes it look uncannily like the Death Star.

answers.name: Rhea
answers.fact: Saturn's second-largest moon, and mostly ice.

answers.name: Iapetus
answers.fact: One hemisphere is nearly black, the other bright white.

answers.name: Dione
answers.fact: Streaked with bright ice cliffs that Voyager mistook for wisps of cloud.

answers.name: Tethys
answers.fact: Carved by Ithaca Chasma, a canyon running most of the way around it.

answers.name: Hyperion
answers.fact: Shaped like a sponge and tumbling chaotically — its rotation can't be predicted.

answers.name: Phoebe
answers.fact: Orbits backwards; probably a captured object from the outer solar system.

answers.name: Prometheus
answers.fact: Steals material from the F ring as it passes.

answers.name: Pandora
answers.fact: Shepherds the other edge of the same ring.

answers.name: Janus
answers.fact: Swaps orbits with Epimetheus every four years.

answers.name: Epimetheus
answers.fact: The other half of that swap — they never actually collide.

answers.name: Pan
answers.fact: Sits inside the Encke Gap and is shaped like a ravioli.

answers.name: Daphnis
answers.fact: Raises standing waves in the ring edges as it passes.
